title: Neurotransmitters and Neuro-hormones
summary: Neurotransmitter types and functions; acetylcholine; steps of neurotransmitter action; neuro-hormones.
revision: Neurotransmitters = chemical messengers across synapses. Steps: synthesis → release → binding → reuptake/breakdown. GABA = inhibitory; Glutamate = excitatory.
confusions: Confusing GABA with glutamate (inhibition vs excitation).

notes.t: A chemical messenger that transmits signals across a synapse from one neuron to another neuron, muscle cell or gland cell.
Neuro-hormones are hormones produced by neurosecretory cells and released into the bloodstream. Examples: ADH and oxytocin (from hypothalamus, released via posterior pituitary).
UGC NET frequently asks about neurotransmitter functions and the steps of synaptic transmission.

mnemonics.title: ADSGG
mnemonics.text: A — Acetylcholine (memory/muscle), D — Dopamine (reward/movement), S — Serotonin (mood/sleep), G — GABA (inhibition), G — Glutamate (excitation)
